To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The optimal MAC design is a Neyman-Peason like design that uses the system information and physical layer measurements; 2) The optimal design can be used as a performance benchmark for other designs; 3) The optimal design leads to a performance gain of 15%-20% over a conventional design that uses only the physical layer measurements; and 4) The gain can be increased by means of multiple physical layer measurements and/or multiple system information measurements.
the MAC layer can be used to improve the performance of the multichannels system and the optimal MAC design can be obtained through the Neyman-Pearon like formulation.
the performance of a MAC protocol can be improved if the system information is utilized in addition to the information obtained from the physical layer measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cross-layer design of multichannel slottedsystems.
the design of a MAC protocol for a wireless multichannel sloted system.

the design of MAC schemes for multichannel reservation systems under Rayleigh fading and is motivated by the need for a better understanding of the performance of such systems in a fading environment.

the proposed MAC design is optimal in the sense of maximizing the channel utilization under a given delay constraint.

we show that a MAC design that utilizes system information in addition of the physical layer measurements can lead to significant gains in performance.
the performance of the MAC layer can be significantly improved by incorporating system information in addition physical layer measurements.
we have provided a framework for the design of cross-layer schemes in multichannel sloted ALOHA systems.

the MAC design problem can be formulated as a detection problem and that the MAC design can be optimized for the performance of the system.
